question: A market research team on the company's Claude for Work plan wants Claude to analyse interview transcripts containing participants' names, employers and health conditions. Which two steps should they take before uploading? Select two.
options: A) Confirm the consent participants gave covers having their transcripts processed in an external tool.
B) Open an incognito chat for the upload so that these health details cannot be retained anywhere at all.
C) Strip out the direct identifiers that the thematic analysis does not actually need in order to work.
D) Divide the transcripts across several separate chats so that no single conversation ever holds them all.
E) Turn off the model improvement setting on the account so the transcripts cannot be used for training.
correct_answers: A) Confirm the consent participants gave covers having their transcripts processed in an external tool.
C) Strip out the direct identifiers that the thematic analysis does not actually need in order to work.
explanations: Correct. Independently of minimisation, health data about identifiable people carries a consent and lawful-basis question that must be settled before processing.
Incognito chats are not used to improve Claude, but they are not a lawful basis for processing sensitive personal data and do not address consent.
Correct. Data minimisation comes first: if the themes can be found without names and employers, that sensitive detail should never be pasted in.
Splitting the same sensitive content across chats does not reduce what was disclosed; it only makes the work harder to manage.
Commercial plans such as Claude for Work do not use inputs or outputs to train models by default, so this changes nothing about the real risk.
